name: InfluxDB
tagline: Purpose-built time-series database, rebuilt in Rust on Arrow, DataFusion and Parquet for version 3.
description: InfluxDB is InfluxData's purpose-built time-series database and probably the most widely deployed one. Version 3 is a ground-up rewrite in Rust on the FDAP stack (Arrow Flight, DataFusion, Arrow, Parquet): writes land in a WAL, are persisted as Parquet on object storage or local disk, and are queried with SQL or InfluxQL. The open-source Core edition (MIT/Apache-2.0) is a single node aimed at recent data, while the commercial Enterprise edition adds clustering, high availability, compaction for long-range queries and RBAC. Teams on 1.x or 2.x should plan a real migration, because Flux is not carried forward into v3.

license.name: MIT or Apache-2.0 (Core); Enterprise is commercial

pricing.notes: Core is free; Enterprise is licensed per deployment (with a free at-home licence); InfluxDB Cloud Serverless is usage-based and Cloud Dedicated is contract-priced.

scale.notes: Core is single-node. Enterprise and InfluxDB Clustered separate ingest, query and compaction nodes over shared object storage.

strengths: Accepts line protocol and the v1/v2 write APIs, so Telegraf and existing agents keep working on v3
Parquet on object storage makes long retention cheap and readable by other Arrow/Parquet tools
Full SQL through Apache DataFusion, plus InfluxQL for existing dashboards
Embedded Python processing engine runs transforms, downsampling and alerts on write or on a schedule
Large ecosystem: Telegraf's 300+ input plugins and first-class Grafana support
weaknesses: Flux is not supported in v3, so 2.x users must rewrite Flux queries in SQL or InfluxQL
Clustering, high availability and long-range compaction are Enterprise-only
Three generations (1.x, 2.x, 3.x) with different APIs and docs cause confusion
No transactions; updates and deletes are coarse compared with a relational database
useCases: Industrial equipment monitoring at the edge
Downsampling and alerting pipelines with Python plugins
notIdealFor: Workloads that rely on Flux scripts
